latin.493: §. III. Spiritualem, Supernaturalem, Cælestemque Modum præsentiæ pariter atque participationis corporis & sanguinis Christi, non alium quempiam, certè non Corporalem, Naturalem ac Terrestrem, Joh. 6., à Christo inculcari, quadruplici argumento probatur.
latin.494: (1) Quia ista duntaxat præsentia corporis & sanguinis, totiusque Christi, commendatur, cujus participes reddimur per spiritualem ad Christum accessum, i. e. per veram vivamque in eum fidem. Ita enim Christus vers. 35. Ego sum panis vitæ: qui ad me venit non esuriet, & qui in me credit, his nunquam sitiet. Et rursus versibus 47. 48. 49. 50. 51. Amen Amen dico vobis qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam. Ego sum panis ille vitæ. Patres vestri ederunt Manna in deserto & mortui sunt. Hic est panis ille qui de cælo descendit, ut qui edit ex eo, non moriatur. Ego sum panis ille vivus qui è Cælo descendi: Si quis ederit ex hoc pane, vivet in æternum. Panis autem quem ego dabo, caro mea est, quam ego dabo pro mundi vita; At per Spiritualem ad Christum accessum fidemque veram ac vivam, non tàm Corporalis corporis & sanguinis Christi quàm Spiritualis potiùs, etiam extra S. Cœnam, reddimur participes.
latin.495: (2) Quia ista duntaxat cùm præsentia, tùm participatio carnis & sanguinis Christi, commendantur, quas certò & infallibiliter spiritualis cum Christo Unio & Communio ipsaque vita æterna & ad hanc à Christo exsuscitatio è mortuis, insequuntur: Nam sic pergit Salvator vers. 53. 54. 55. 56. Amen Amen dico vobis, nisi ederitis carnem Filii hominis & biberitis ejus Sanguinem, non habebitis vitam in vobis. Qui edit carnem meam & bibit meum sanguinem, habet vitam æternam, & ego suscitabo ipsum ultimo illo die. Caro enim mea verè est cibus & sanguis meus verè est potus, qui edit meam carnem & bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet & ego in eo. At effectus hi Spirituales, Supernaturales & Cælestes, non nisi Spirituali Christi Præsentiæ & Participationi, indivisim ac necessariò adhærent, non Corporali aut Orali, uti in confesso est, & ex indignorum manducatione sacramentali quidem, etiam orali, ex Lutheranorum hypothesi, at spiritualis vacua, liquidò constat.
latin.496: (3) Quia ista solummodò præsentia cum participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi commendatur, quæ etiam cum adscensu corporis Christi in cælum, probè consistere, quin ex adscensu corporis Christi in Cœlum, contra discipulos, manducationi carnis ejus & sanguinis, dum coram adhuc adesset, in terris intercedentes ac obluctati, evinci hisce Christi verbis poterat: Quid si igitur spectaveritis Filium Hominis adscendentem eo, ubi erat priùs? vers. 62. At non Corporalis in terris præsentia ex adscensu corporis Christi in Cœlum, sed Spiritualis tantùm, colligi demonstrarique in promptu erat. Proptereà adscensionis suæ meminit, inquit Athanasius: hina somatikēs ennoias autous aphelkysēi — eos, à corporali intellectu abstraheret & ut deinceps carnem suam cœlestem & spiritualem cibum esse discerent, Tom. I. tract. in illud: Qui dixerit verbum contra Spir. S.
latin.497: (4) Quia Carnalis seu Corporalis corporis aut carnis Christi Participatio nulli omnino usui esse disertè à Christo perhibetur, quando murmurantibus adhuc Discipulis & sibi durum paulò antè visum verbum nec tum quidem absque indignatione transmittentibus, ipse tandem pertinaciori obmurmurationi finem impositurus & pessulum obditurus vers. 63. respondet: Spiritus est qui vivificat, caro non prodest quicquam. Verba quæ ego loquor vobis, spiritus & vita sunt; Hisce verbis, vel binâ ratione expressa, Carnalem Præsentiam ac Participationem Carnis & Sanguinis sui suppressurus, erectis & in apricum positis solis Spiritualibus: primò quidem, dum carnem suam, non equidem per se spectatam, sed carnaliter manducandam (de qua sola hactenus disputatio, se inter & Judæos partim, partim Christianos discipulos suos, intercesserat) nihil prodesse ait, interpretante sic verba Augustino, Serm. secundô de Verbis Domini & suffragante Paschasio: Sine Spiritu S. inquit sicut nec caro Christi prodest quicquam, ita nec hoc Sacramentum Christi prodesse potest lib. 3. de Corp. & Sangv. Christi, i. e. Corpus Christi non prodest quicquam, non per se, sed per accidens & aliud, quod impedit illius Operationem, ut ipsi Lutherani, Lutherô contra Carlstadium præeunte, non possunt non fateri, quia sine fide Christus & Evangelium non tantum nihil prosunt, sed nocent, sunt odor mortis & judicium Dei accelerant. Unde Brentius in Exegesi Johannis: Verum equidem est, ait, carnem Christi comesam, quomodo Capernaitæ intellexerunt, dentibus laceratam, nihil prodesse, prodest autem plurimùm mysterio fidei & dentibus cordis accepta.
latin.498: Dehinc verò, dum verba, de carne sua & sanguine participandis, à se prolixius edisserta, non propriè & carnaliter, sed mysticè ac spiritualiter, tum intelligenda, tùm in effectum danda, pronunciat: Verba quæ loquor, Spiritus & vita sunt; Quasi dicat, Cur hâc mea loquendi ratione offendimini? Et vos ignoratis, spiritualiter esse intelligenda, non carnaliter, quæ de carnis meæ locutus sum manducatione? Non enim de corporis alimento, adeoque de carne, corporis mei parte, hôc loco sermo erat, sed de nutritione spirituali, eamque sequente conjunctione vestri, ceu membrorum, mecum capite, vers. 63. de Vita vestra per me, quæ temporalis non est, sed æterna vers. 57. ad quam vos suscitaturus sum ultimâ die: ita Spiritus, i. e. sensus spiritualiter sumtus verbaque rectè intellecta vivificant, Caro verò, verbaque carnaliter & crassè accepta, nil prosunt. Cum ergo verba mea Spiritus sint, deq; spiritualibus agam, cùm de vita non temporali sed æterna, nutritioneque mystica, quâ in unum coalescimus corpus, ego loquar, cur crassum & carnalem mihi affingitis sensum?

pass_a.493: §. III. That the Spiritual, Supernatural, and Celestial Mode of presence alike and of participation of Christ’s body and blood — not any other, certainly not the Corporal, Natural and Earthly — is inculcated by Christ in John 6, is proved by a fourfold argument.
pass_a.494: (1) Because that presence alone of body and blood, and of whole Christ, is commended, of which we are made partakers by spiritual access to Christ, i.e. by true and living faith in Him. So Christ at v. 35: I am the bread of life: who comes to me shall not hunger, and who believes in me shall never thirst. And again vv. 47–51 … But by spiritual access to Christ and true living faith we are made partakers not so much of a Corporal as rather of a Spiritual body and blood of Christ, even outside the Sacred Supper.
pass_a.495: (2) Because that presence and participation of Christ’s flesh and blood alone are commended, which spiritual Union and Communion with Christ and eternal life itself and raising from the dead by Christ unto it certainly and infallibly follow … But these Spiritual, Supernatural and Celestial effects adhere inseparably and necessarily only to Spiritual Presence and Participation of Christ, not to Corporal or Oral — as is confessed, and as is clear from the sacramental, even oral, eating of the unworthy which on the Lutheran hypothesis is empty of the spiritual.
pass_a.496: (3) Because that presence with participation of Christ’s body and blood alone is commended which also rightly consists with the ascent of Christ’s body into heaven — nay, from the ascent into Heaven against disciples who, while He was still present on earth, interposed and struggled against eating His flesh and blood, could be proved by these words of Christ: What then if you should see the Son of Man ascending where He was before? (v. 62). But not Corporal presence on earth from the ascent of Christ’s body into Heaven, but Spiritual only, was ready to be gathered and demonstrated. Therefore He mentions His ascension, says Athanasius — that He might draw them away from corporal intellect and that thereafter they might learn His flesh to be heavenly and spiritual food.
pass_a.497: (4) Because carnal or corporal Participation of Christ’s body or flesh is expressly declared by Christ to be of no use at all, when with disciples still murmuring and not even then transmitting without indignation the word that seemed hard a little earlier, He at last about to put an end to more stubborn murmuring and bolt the door answers at v. 63: It is the Spirit that quickens, the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit and life … Augustine and Paschasius: without the Holy Spirit as Christ’s flesh profits nothing, so neither can this Sacrament of Christ profit … Brentius: flesh of Christ eaten as the Capernaites understood, torn with teeth, profits nothing; but profits much received by the mystery of faith and the teeth of the heart.
pass_a.498: Then, while He pronounces the words He had more fully set forth about participating His flesh and blood to be understood not properly and carnally but mystically and spiritually, and so to be put into effect: The words that I speak are Spirit and life — as if to say, Why are you offended at this manner of speaking of mine? And do you not know that what I spoke of eating my flesh is to be understood spiritually, not carnally? For the discourse here was not of bodily food and so of flesh as a part of my body, but of spiritual nutrition and the following conjunction of you as members with me the head … So Spirit, i.e. sense taken spiritually and words rightly understood, quicken; but Flesh, and words accepted carnally and coarsely, profit nothing. Since therefore my words are Spirit, and I treat of spiritual things, of life not temporal but eternal, and of mystical nutrition whereby we coalesce into one body, why do you fasten a coarse and carnal sense upon me?

493: §.III: four proofs that in John 6 Christ inculcates the Spiritual, Supernatural, Celestial Mode of presence and participation of His body and blood.
Not any other mode — certainly not the Corporal, Natural, Earthly one.
494: (1) The only presence of body, blood, and whole Christ that is recommended is the one we share by spiritual access — true living faith (John 6:35, 47–51).
By that faith we partake spiritually rather than corporally — even outside the Sacred Supper.
495: (2) The presence and participation recommended are those which spiritual union with Christ, eternal life, and the last-day raising infallibly follow (John 6:53–56).
Those heavenly effects cling only to spiritual presence and participation — not corporal or oral; even on the Lutheran view the unworthy’s oral eating is spiritually empty.
496: (3) The recommended presence must also stand with Christ’s bodily ascent into heaven (John 6:62) — so from the ascent one gathers spiritual presence on earth, not corporal.
Athanasius: He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect and teach His flesh as heavenly spiritual food. (Greek transliterated in Pass B.)
497: (4) Carnal or corporal participation of Christ’s flesh is of no use at all (John 6:63): the Spirit quickens; the flesh profits nothing; His words are spirit and life.

Augustine and Paschasius: without the Spirit neither flesh nor sacrament profits; Lutherans admit Christ without faith harms; Brentius: Capernaite tooth-tearing profits nothing — faith’s heart-teeth do.
498: Second half of (4): understand the flesh-and-blood words mystically and spiritually — Spirit and life — not as bodily food of a body-part, but spiritual nutrition joining members to the Head, eternal life and last-day raising.
Spiritually taken sense quickens; carnal coarse hearing profits nothing — why fasten a thick carnal sense on spiritual speech?
Stop before §.IV (antecedent Institution commentary hands off to the Pauline / Apostolic successor).
